programme: A trio of parallel signal-responsive transcription factor axes converging on the same output genes: TEAD4 (Hippo–YAP/TAZ effector; targets HIF1A, VEGFA, VEGFB, and the cardiac/mechanotransduction genes MYH7 and CCN2), ELK4 (Ras–ERK/SRF ternary-complex factor; targets the immediate-early proliferative/survival genes EGR1, FOS, MCL1), and ATF2 (stress-MAPK/AP-1 effector; targets the endothelial-activation/inflammatory genes IL6, TNF, PTGS2, NOS2, SELE). ZBTB2 sits alongside them, coupling p53 status to HIF-1 hypoxia signaling and reinforcing the angiogenic/hypoxic arm that TEAD4 also touches.
role_in_a: In vascular/cardiac tissue this axis is the classical route from mechanical and hypoxic stress to pathological remodeling: TEAD4–YAP/TAZ mechanotransduction driving cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and angiogenic response (its own target set includes the sarcomere gene MYH7 and the fibrotic gene CCN2/CTGF), ELK4–SRF immediate-early signaling driving vascular smooth-muscle proliferation after injury, and ATF2/AP-1 driving the endothelial-activation programme (IL6, TNF, PTGS2, NOS2, SELE) central to atherosclerotic inflammation. None of this is supported by anything retrieved for this pair — it is standard vascular/cardiac biology asserted from outside the record, since Open Targets and literature search returned nothing for any of the twelve factors in cardiovascular disease.
role_in_b: In lung cancer each of the four carrying factors has direct, if uneven, retrieved support: TEAD4 sits at a high Open Targets percentile (0.78) consistent with the well-known oncogenic YAP/TEAD axis, though its two cited PMIDs are the same ones cited for ELK4 and are flagged uncertain for TEAD4 specifically; ELK4 promotes MSI2-mediated NSCLC progression via TGF-β signaling (PMID 39969091) and is implicated via a tRNA-fragment/HSPB1-MED29 mechanism (PMID 35526007); ATF2 drives NSCLC invasion through the JNK-ATF2/c-Jun-MMP2/9 axis (PMID 37964204) and is targeted by an anticancer compound active in NSCLC (PMID 39215681); ZBTB2 links p53 loss to HIF-1-driven hypoxic aggressiveness in cancer (PMID 36341521).
shared_axis: Both tissues route growth-factor, mechanical and hypoxic stress through the same Hippo-YAP/TEAD, Ras-ERK/ETS and stress-MAPK/AP-1 transcription factor families onto an overlapping angiogenic-proliferative-inflammatory gene set; chronic vascular injury/hypoxia in cardiovascular disease and hypoxic tumor growth in lung cancer would each be expected to engage this same stress-responsive TF set, without either disease needing to cause the other.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally coherent (three parallel signal-responsive TF families converging on angiogenic/proliferative/inflammatory targets), and the lung-cancer side is backed by retrieved papers for three of the four carrying factors. But nothing retrieved places any factor in cardiovascular disease, so the CVD arm of the story rests entirely on general vascular/cardiac biology rather than on anything in the record, which caps this below 'strong'.
support: PMID 39969091 — ELK4 promotes MSI2-mediated NSCLC progression via TGF-β (also cited, ambiguously, under TEAD4); PMID 35526007 — tRNA fragment drives NSCLC via HSPB1/MED29 (also cited, ambiguously, under TEAD4); PMID 39215681 — a novel compound shows anticancer activity in NSCLC via an ATF2-related mechanism; PMID 37964204 — ANKRD49 promotes NSCLC metastasis via the JNK-ATF2/c-Jun-MMP2/9 axis; PMID 36341521 — ZBTB2 links p53 deficiency to HIF-1-driven hypoxia signaling and cancer aggressiveness. None found for cardiovascular disease for any factor.
how_to_falsify: Perturb each factor individually (verteporfin or dominant-negative TEAD to block YAP-TEAD4; ERK-pathway inhibition or ELK4 knockdown; JNK inhibition or ATF2 knockdown) in parallel in (a) human coronary/vascular endothelial or smooth-muscle cells under hypoxic or oxidized-LDL stress and (b) NSCLC lines, and check whether the matched target signature collapses in both systems (VEGFA/HIF1A for TEAD4, EGR1/FOS for ELK4, IL6/TNF/PTGS2/SELE for ATF2). If the lung-cancer signature responds but the vascular signature does not, the cardiovascular arm of this account is wrong and the concordance seen here is not driven by this programme.
caveats: No cardiovascular-disease evidence — Open Targets or literature — was retrieved for any of the twelve factors, so role_in_a is asserted from general biology, not from this record. TEAD4's two cited PMIDs are shared with ELK4's and are explicitly flagged as uncertain for TEAD4. No paper addressed both diseases together. The 224 patient-group comparisons derive from only 2 independent cohort pairs. Tissue-generic immune/nuclear-receptor regulators (BCL3, RELB, NFATC1, RARA, ID2/ID3, PBX1, GFI1B, TFE3, BCL6, FOXO4, SMAD4) were already stripped out before ranking, so this account deliberately does not reach for one of those as a tissue master regulator. HDAC3/NCoR1 (a genuine corepressor complex), RFXANK/NFX1 (MHC-II-linked, sharing HLA-E/HLA-DRA targets), ISL1, TADA2A, ZNF224 and RAX were concordant in this pair but belong to different, unrelated mechanisms and are left out of this programme rather than forced in.
